cosy-lesson.title: Your Brain Can Keep Improving Into Your 90s

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Plasticity – the ability of the brain to change and adapt over time.

p.em: Example: Adult neurogenesis is clear evidence of brain plasticity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Improve – to make or become better in quality, strength, or ability.

p.em: Example: Reading daily is an easy way to improve your memory.

cosy-blockquote.p: Elder – an older person, especially one who is highly respected.

p.em: Example: Elders play an essential role in preserving family history.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive – relating to the mental processes of perception and memory.

p.em: Example: Solving puzzles helps maintain strong cognitive functions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Stimulus – something that causes a reaction or activity in an organism.

p.em: Example: A complex visual stimulus keeps the brain active.

cosy-blockquote.p: Memory – the faculty by which the mind stores and recalls information.

p.em: Example: Her grandmother has an exceptionally sharp memory.

cosy-blockquote.p: Habit – a settled or regular tendency or practice.

p.em: Example: Learning a language is a wonderful mental habit for seniors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Active ≠ Passive – participating in activities or physical exercise ≠ not active; receiving or submitting to an action without responding.

p.em: Example: Seniors who stay active have much better brain health than those with passive routines.

cosy-blockquote.p: Science – the intellectual and practical study of the physical world.

p.em: Example: Modern science shows that our brains can grow new cells.

cosy-blockquote.p: Capacity – the maximum amount that something can contain or produce.

p.em: Example: Our mental capacity does not have to decline as we age.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, how does the discovery of adult brain plasticity change classical medical beliefs about old age?
★ What daily habits do you think are most important for keeping your mind sharp?

What evidence is presented in the study to prove that senior citizens can continue to improve their memories in their 90s?
★ Have you ever tried learning a new language or instrument just for fun?

Based on the research findings, how does a respected elder benefit from participating in high-contrast visual tasks?
★ Who is the oldest person you know, and how do they stay active?

According to the paper, what parameters explain how complex cognitive stimuli trigger dendritic branching?
★ Do you prefer doing puzzles, reading, or playing physical sports to challenge yourself?

What data in the article suggests that exposing the brain to a new stimulus triggers the growth of fresh neural connections?
★ How do you handle forgetfulness or minor memory slips in your daily life?

According to researchers, how can a senior develop a strong memory reserve even after decades of inactivity?
★ Do you find that physical exercise helps you think more clearly?

Based on the text, why does building a daily learning habit provide better neurological shielding than passive rest?
★ What is a complex skill you learned recently that took a lot of mental effort?

What evidence in the study proves that staying mentally and physically active actually reverses brain shrinkage?
★ Do you think modern technology makes our brains lazier or more active?

How does modern science measure structural cellular changes in senescent hippocampal regions?
★ How often do you step out of your comfort zone to try something completely new?

According to the article, why is the brain's capacity for growth essentially unlimited if properly stimulated?
★ What is your favorite way to wind down and give your brain a deep rest?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this hypothesis, biological guidelines will prove that adult brain plasticity is active until our final days.
★ Would you take a daily pill if it guaranteed your brain would stay 20 years younger?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, we will use specialized optical lenses to directly improve senior visual processing.
★ Do you think society treats elderly people as wise contributors or as a burden?

Imagine future research shows that every elder can grow new hippocampal cells, retirement communities will replace standard care with academic lecture halls.
★ If you lived to be 100, what kind of project or hobby would you like to pursue?

If future research proves this discovery beyond doubt, doctors will prescribe cognitive complexity tests over traditional physical reflexes for elderly licenses.
★ Should there be a mandatory retirement age, or should people work as long as they want?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, targeted electric stimulus waves will be used to restore lost memory functions.
★ Would you allow a brain chip to monitor and optimize your cognitive speed?

Imagine future research proves that memory decays only due to boredom, how would families design multi-generational households?
★ How do you hope to maintain your mental independence when you get older?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, senior citizens will maintain a highly active professional career well into their 90s.
★ Do you think future technology will make retirement homes completely obsolete?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, medical science will map the exact genetic link between optimism and dendritic branching.
★ What is the most important piece of wisdom you want to pass down to future generations?

Imagine future research proves that our mental capacity is physically doubled when we teach others, senior center volunteers will receive national honors.
★ Do you believe that wisdom only comes with old age, or can young people be wise too?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, we will verify that a daily habit of speaking a foreign language halts dementia by 80%.
★ How has your own perspective on aging changed over the last ten years?

ul.li: Incorrect: My grandfather is 90 years → Correct: My grandfather is 90 years old ((Specify 'old' or omit))
Incorrect: I hope to live until 100 → Correct: I hope to live to 100 ((Use 'to' for age limits))
Incorrect: It depend of your genes → Correct: It depends on your genes ((Preposition 'on' after depend))
